gap: No result ChatGPT got states a figure measured by a named reviewer near cooktop power. The Technology Man got 907 Wh in about 54 minutes from an Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at a steady 1 kW, and the same unit overheated and shut down after 26 minutes on a 2 kW heater. CleanTechnica watched a BLUETTI AC180 hold a 1,500 W induction burner on high.
standout_why: I checked the cited BLUETTI AC200L page (bluettipower.com/pages/ac200l). It has only spec-sheet numbers and a worked example that assumes 90% DoD × 90% efficiency, with no tests and no mention of induction. ChatGPT's own answer assumes 85% and runs that through its table and calculator (2,048 Wh at 1,500 W gives 1 h 10 min). I could not open the other cited rival, unpluggedwatts.com, because of a TLS certificate error, so I can't say whether it has measured data. The pages I opened that do measure (OutdoorGearLab, Notebookcheck, StorageReview, The Technology Man, CleanTechnica) found 82–89% usable at light or unstated loads. Only The Technology Man and CleanTechnica tested a 1 kWh-class unit at 1–2 kW, which is cooktop level.
decides: It argues against putting an 1,800 W plate on an 1,800–2,000 W, 1 kWh-class unit, which our page currently rates 'at its limit' or 'small headroom'. The C1000 Gen 2, rated 2,000 W, overheated after 26 minutes at 2 kW, and measured usable energy in this class is 850–950 Wh, so an 1,800 W plate gets about 30 minutes at most. That supports leading with the 2 kWh, 2,600 W-plus units (Elite 200 V2 and DJI Power 2000, or Elite 300) for real cooking. It also confirms the AC180 is fine with a 1,500 W plate, since CleanTechnica measured it holding 1,500 W on high.

findings.label: Usable AC energy at a steady 1 kW load (The Technology Man)
findings.value: 907 Wh in just over 54 min (about 89% of 1,024 Wh)
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (Gidon, 2025-11-04)
findings.note: Constant 1 kW resistive electric heater, measured with an energy-monitoring plug. Arithmetic: 907 Wh ÷ 1,800 W ≈ 30 min for an 1,800 W plate at full power. US unit.

findings.label: Sustained near-rated load (The Technology Man)
findings.value: Overheated and shut down after 26 min on a 2,000 W heater
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (Gidon, 2025-11-04)
findings.note: The reviewer says the heater sat too close to the unit, which probably made it worse. Beyond 2,000 W the output dropped to 2,000 W, then an overload error cut AC and it came back after about 30 s. The inverter drew about 17 W with no load.

findings.label: Measured usable AC capacity (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.source_title: The 14 Best Portable Power Stations, OutdoorGearLab (RJ Spurrier et al., updated 2026-07-23)

findings.label: AC discharge efficiency at 1,800 W, EU 230 V version (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: Just over 92% at 1,800 W; about 2,650 Wh (just under 88%) at a little over 200 W
findings.source_title: 3 kWh in a compact package: Powerstation Bluetti Elite 300 review (Marcus Schwarten, 2026-03-09, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: This is the only named measurement I found at exactly an induction-plate wattage. EU unit; the US version differs. Arithmetic: 3,014.4 Wh × 0.92 ≈ 2,770 Wh ÷ 1,800 W ≈ 92 min. Over 50 dB at 1 m under load.

findings.label: Sustained cooking-class load (CleanTechnica)
findings.value: Air fryer drawing 1,482 W (12 A at 119.7 V) for 15 min; Keurig at 1,345 W
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Test & Review, CleanTechnica (Z. S., 2025-07-07)
findings.note: Battery went from 56% to 45% over the air-fryer run. That 11% of 2,073.6 Wh is about 228 Wh, less than 1,482 W × 0.25 h = 370 Wh, so the element was cycling and you can't get a runtime from it. No Wh delivered or efficiency reported.

findings.label: AC discharge, EU 230 V version (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: Just under 920 Wh (just under 90%) at about 250 W
findings.source_title: Affordable power station for camping, emergency power and more: Oscal PowerMax 1800 SE review (Marcus Schwarten, 2026-09-26)
findings.note: The display read 350 W while the actual load was about 250 W. With AC and Wi-Fi on and no load, it drained fully in about 1.5 days. Notebookcheck says it can't run several high-power devices at once.

findings.label: Combined load over 30 A outlet (CleanTechnica)
findings.value: Close to 2,900 W total with no errors
findings.source_title: DJI Power 2000 Portable Power Station — CleanTechnica Tested (Jennifer Sensiba, 2025-08-25)
findings.note: AC unit, fridge, lights and short microwave bursts ran for about 2 h. No Wh delivered was measured, and the 2 h can't mean 2,900 W sustained, so the average load was much lower.
